Python Foundations Project: Austo¶

Problem Statement¶

Context¶

In the 21st century, cars are an important mode of transportation that provides us the opportunity for personal control and autonomy. In day-to-day life, people use cars for commuting to work, shopping, visiting family and friends, etc. Research shows that more than 76% of people prevent themselves from traveling somewhere if they don't have a car. Most people tend to buy different types of cars based on their day-to-day necessities and preferences. So, it is essential for automobile companies to analyze the preference of their customers before launching a car model into the market. Austo, a UK-based automobile company aspires to grow its business into the US market after successfully establishing its footprints in the European market.

In order to be familiar with the types of cars preferred by the customers and factors influencing the car purchase behavior in the US market, Austo has contracted a consulting firm. Based on various market surveys, the consulting firm has created a dataset of 3 major types of cars that are extensively used across the US market. They have collected various details of the car owners which can be analyzed to understand the automobile market of the US.

Objective¶

Austo's management team wants to understand the demand of the buyers and trends in the US market. They want to build customer profiles based on the analysis to identify new purchase opportunities so that they can manipulate the business strategy and production to meet certain demand levels. Further, the analysis will be a good way for management to understand the dynamics of a new market. Suppose you are a Data Scientist working at the consulting firm that has been contracted by Austo. You are given the task to create buyer's profiles for different types of cars with the available data as well as a set of recommendations for Austo. Perform the data analysis to generate useful insights that will help the automobile company to grow its business.

Data Description¶

austo_automobile.csv: The dataset contains buyer's data corresponding to different types of products(cars).

Data Dictionary¶

  • Age: Age of the customer
  • Gender: Gender of the customer
  • Profession: Indicates whether the customer is a salaried or business person
  • Marital_status: Marital status of the customer
  • Education: Refers to the highest level of education completed by the customer
  • No_of_dependents: Number of dependents(partner/children/spouse) of the customer
  • Personal_loan: Indicates whether the customer availed a personal loan or not
  • House_loan: Indicates whether the customer availed house loan or not
  • Partner_working: Indicates whether the customer's partner is working or not
  • Salary: Annual Salary of the customer
  • Partner_salary: Annual Salary of the customer's partner
  • Total_salary: Annual household income (Salary + Partner_salary) of the customer's family
  • Price: Price of the car
  • Make: Car type (Hatchback/Sedan/SUV)

Observations:¶

Numeric Columns:

  • Age: As noticiable in the bar chart, the age is centered around young adults between 20 to 30, followed by 30 to 40.
  • No_of_Dependents: Mostly about 2-3 dependents.
  • Salary: I notice a slight right-skew where more people are at lower salaries.
  • Partner_salary: A spike at 0 indicate many single income households.
  • Total_salary: Wider spread than Salary possibly because it may include two earners in some cases.
  • Price: From earlier statistical summary, min 18,000; mean = 35,598; max 70,000. A wide range indicates both entry and higher-end models. This is graph is better representation unlike my earlier assumption that the cars are priced more from mid to high end.

Categorical Columns:

  • Gender: It is clearly a male dominated buyers market.
  • Profession: Salaried is higher than Business.
  • Marital_status: Married is the largest indicating mostly family purchases.
  • Education: Dominance in Post Graduate buyers indicates an educated buyer base.
  • Personal_loan / House_loan: Personal loans are more common than House loans. May need more analysis to understand financing offers attractiveness.
  • Partner_working: No is higher indicating many households are single-income and this correlates to the Partner_salary spiked at 0.
  • Make: The dataset is imbalanced from counts: Hatchback = 884, Sedan = 460, SUV = 237 (where Hatchbacks dominate).

Question 8: How many owners have bought cars that were priced higher than their salary. How many of them have taken personal loan? [3 marks]¶

In [95]:
# Cars where price > owner's salary
cars_price_gt_salary = df[df["Price"] > df["Salary"]]

# Total number of such owners
owners_price_gt_salary = cars_price_gt_salary.shape[0]
print("Total owners who bought cars priced higher than their salary:", owners_price_gt_salary)

# Out of them, how many took a personal loan
owners_with_loan = cars_price_gt_salary[cars_price_gt_salary["Personal_loan"] == "Yes"].shape[0]
print("\nOwners (Price > Salary) who took a personal loan:", owners_with_loan)

# Calculate percentages
total_owners_percentage = (owners_price_gt_salary / len(df)) * 100
loan_percentage = (owners_with_loan / owners_price_gt_salary) * 100

print("\nPercentage of all buyers who purchased cars above their salary:", round(total_owners_percentage, 2), '%')
print("\nPercentage of those buyers who used a personal loan:", round(loan_percentage, 2), '%')

Total owners who bought cars priced higher than their salary: 96

Owners (Price > Salary) who took a personal loan: 44

Percentage of all buyers who purchased cars above their salary: 6.07 %

Percentage of those buyers who used a personal loan: 45.83 %

Observations:¶

  • Only 6% purchased cars priced higher than their annual salary.
  • Among these 46% owners used a personal loan to afford the car, while the remaining managed without a personal loan.
  • This suggests that while most buyers purchase cars within their income range, a small fraction still spends beyond their earnings capacity, and almost half of them rely on personal loans to do so.

# 5. Correlation heatmap for all numerical variables
numeric_cols = ["Age", "No_of_Dependents", "Salary", "Partner_salary", "Total_salary", "Price"]

plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
sns.heatmap(df[numeric_cols].corr(), annot=True, cmap="Blues", fmt=".2f")
plt.title("Correlation Heatmap (Numeric Variables)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Observations:¶

  1. Price vs Age (scatterplot)
  • There is no strong linear trend.
  • Cars are bought across all age groups, but younger buyers (20s–30s) seem to prefer lower-priced cars, while some older buyers spend more on expensive cars indicating financial stability and higher incomes in later stage of life.
  • A dense cluster of points in the lower priced cars indicate this segment is popular across all age groups.
  1. Price vs Total Salary (scatterplot)
  • A positive trend: as total salary increases, car price also tends to increase.
  • However, a few outliers exist — some lower salary buyers purchased high-priced cars (likely using loans) and some buyers with higher salaries purchased lower priced cars.
  1. Price by Car Make (boxplot)
  • Hatchbacks dominate in count (884 cars, ~56%) but are mostly concentrated in the lower price range and have the lowest median price around 22,000 - 24,000 that are good budget cars.
  • SUVs have the highest median prices hence can be positioned as luxury or premium cars.
  • Sedan median falls in the mid range in comparision to these other two options serving as a mid segment option.
  1. Price by Profession (boxplot)
  • Business owners have a wider price spread with fewer purchases, and occasionally tend to purchase higher-priced cars compared to salaried individuals.
  • Salaried individuals are more consistent in their spending and generally purchase cars in the lower to mid price ranges.
  1. Correlation Heatmap (numeric variables)
  • Age shows strong positve correlation to Price indicating older customers purchasing more expensive cars.
  • Total_salary has a strong positive correlation with Salary (as expected, since Total_salary includes Salary + Partner_salary).
  • Price shows a moderate positive correlation with Total_salary, confirming that higher-earning households tend to buy more expensive cars.
  • Age and Price have very weak correlation, meaning age is not a strong predictor of car price in this dataset.
  • Dependents shows very weak or negative correlations. Family size does not impact car price decisions.

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 12: Write the conclusions and business recommendations derived from the analysis. (6 marks)¶

Conclusions

  • Age is an important aspect: Younger buyers (20–30) mostly choose budget Hatchbacks, while older buyers (40–60) lean toward higher-priced SUVs and Sedans. Age shows stronger influence on price than income.
  • Car type distribution: Hatchbacks dominate (884 cars, ~56%), concentrated in the 18k–30k range. Sedans form the mid-tier (30k–50k), while SUVs occupy the premium segment (50k–70k).
  • Profession patterns: Salaried buyers are more predictable, usually buying in the mid-price range, while business owners are split. Some buy budget cars, others invest in premium SUVs. Salaried buyers also spend slightly more on average.
  • Income influence: Higher salaries generally correspond to higher-priced cars, though the link is moderate. Many buyers in the 40k–80k household income band prefer cars priced 20k–40k.
  • Loans & affordability: Around 6% buy cars above their salary; almost 46% of them rely on personal loans. Even customers with both home and personal loans still purchase cars (~30k–32k range), showing financing is important and preferred by many.

Business Recommendations for Austo

  1. Segmented Product Strategy
  • Budget Segment (18,000 - 30,000 Hatchbacks):
    • Target younger buyers (20 to 30 years), mostly salaried professionals starting out.
    • Also since Hatchbacks dominate sales (~56%) that price range, Austo should focus on this segment for volume growth, positioning Hatchbacks as affordable, reliable first cars for younger buyers.
    • Focus on affordability, fuel efficiency, and compact design.
  • Mid-Segment (30,000 - 50,000 Sedans):
    • Position Sedans for salaried mid-income households (40,000 - 80,000 income).
    • Highlight comfort, safety, and value for money.
  • Premium Segment (50,000 - 70,000 SUVs):
    • Market SUVs to older buyers (40 to 60 years) and high-income families (>100k income).
    • Highlight luxury, technology, and status appeal.
  1. Profession-Based Targeting
  • Salaried professionals: Offer affordable EMIs for Sedans and SUVs, since they show consistent mid-price spending habits.
  • Business professionals: Create dual strategies — budget Hatchbacks for conservative buyers, and premium SUVs for luxury buyers.
  1. Loan & Financing Solutions
  • Expand loan/EMI options for buyers stretching beyond income.
  • Custom packages: flexible for business owners, affordable EMIs for salaried
  1. Marketing
  • Age based campaigns:
    • Young (20 to 30): “First car” Hatchback focus.
    • Older (40 to 60): Premium SUV/Sedan lifestyle branding.
  • Highlight finance friendly options to attract buyers hesitant due to loans or limited income.
  1. Strategic Takeaway
  • Austo should leverage Hatchbacks for volume, Sedans for mid market stability, and SUVs for high margin premium sales.
  • A balanced portfolio targeting both income based and age based segments will help maximize market share in the US.
